steps.title: If a pop-up says your computer is locked and to call a number, it is a scam
steps.detail: Close the browser. If it will not close, restart the computer.
steps.why: Real companies do not lock your screen and ask you to call.
steps.do_not: Do not call the number and do not let anyone connect to your computer.

steps.title: If files have strange names or a ransom note appears, stop
steps.detail: That is ransomware, not a frozen computer. Unplug the network cable, turn off Wi-Fi, leave the computer on and open the ransomware plan.
steps.why: Ransomware needs different steps, and the first minutes matter.
steps.do_not: Do not restart or switch off the computer.

steps.title: Windows: close the stuck app with Task Manager
steps.detail: Right-click the Start button, choose Task Manager, select the app that is not responding and click End task. Then open it again.
steps.why: This closes only the stuck app, not the whole computer.
steps.source_name: Microsoft: Outlook for Windows not responding

steps.title: Mac: force the stuck app to quit
steps.detail: Press Option, Command and Esc together, choose the app and click Force Quit. If the whole Mac does not respond, restart it.
steps.why: This closes only the stuck app.
steps.source_name: Apple: How to force an app to quit on Mac

steps.title: When it works again, install updates
steps.detail: Install waiting updates for the computer and the app that froze.
steps.why: Updates fix many crashes and security holes.

steps.title: Still stuck? Call your IT contact
steps.detail: Tell them what you tried and what you see on screen. A photo of the screen helps.
steps.why: They can check settings and equipment you cannot reach.
